content: Laravel 11 documents insertOrIgnore as ignoring duplicate insert errors but warns that other database-engine errors may also be ignored and that MySQL strict mode is bypassed; upsert inserts missing records and updates matching records, requires unique indexes except SQL Server, and MySQL and MariaDB use the table unique indexes rather than the conflict-column argument. Because existing sender labels must remain untouched, an update-capable upsert is the wrong primitive; a unique-index-backed insert-ignore plus a pair lookup is the relevant direction, with the warning caveat covered by best-effort logging and tests. Source: official Laravel 11 Query Builder documentation.
